executive-summary.context: Week 1 optimizations delivered 2-10× speedup (Bloom pre-filter). Week 2 targets additional 4-7× compound speedup via two optimizations: SIMD text hashing (2-8×) + Batch LSH lookups (1.3-2×).

simd-text-hashing.rationale: Generic reusable primitive for whitespace-tokenized text across projects
simd-text-hashing.reusability: ML preprocessing, log parsing, search indexing, corpus generation, deduplication

batch-lsh-lookups.rationale: LSH-specific optimization, not a generic primitive
batch-lsh-lookups.coupling: Tightly coupled to MinHashSignatureCapsule + LSH bucket structure
batch-lsh-lookups.alternative: Extract generic BatchQuery<T> trait later if pattern proves broadly valuable

q1-real-problem.identified: Token generation bottleneck: 35% of corpus generation time @ 3.5M docs/sec (scalar whitespace split + hash)
LSH lookup overhead: O(L × n) per query (L=5 tables, n=avg bucket size ~50-100 docs)
q1-real-problem.baseline: Week 1: 3.5M docs/sec generation, 912K docs/sec dedup @ 16 cores

q2-correctness.simd-text: Must preserve exact token semantics (whitespace split, FNV-1a hash, deterministic output)
q2-correctness.batch-lsh: Must maintain LSH recall (92-99% for L=5 tables, no degradation)
q2-correctness.property-tests: SIMD equivalence tests (10K random texts vs scalar baseline), Batch recall tests (ground truth comparison)

q4-constraints.determinism: Exact output match (SIMD vs scalar, batch vs sequential)
q4-constraints.memory: Zero-copy where possible (SIMD in-place, batch Vec pooling)

q5-dependencies.new: portable_simd (nightly, already used in Week 1 SIMD MinHash)
q5-dependencies.zero-new-crates: Both optimizations use existing dependencies (no new crates)

q6-scale.lsh-buckets: L=5 tables × ~1M unique buckets, avg 50-100 docs per bucket

simd-text.reason: Vectorize string ops (whitespace scan + hash), moderate SIMD expertise

batch-lsh.reason: Amortize lookups (parallel bucket queries), straightforward rayon parallelism

integration.reason: Both extend existing APIs (minimal breaking changes)

q8-data-characteristics.lsh-buckets: Collision chains (avg 50-100 docs), power-law distribution (few large buckets, many small)
q8-data-characteristics.access-pattern: Sequential text scan (SIMD-friendly), random LSH bucket access (hash table lookup)

q9-edge-cases.simd-text: Empty strings (0 tokens), single-word docs (1 token, no SIMD benefit), unicode edge cases
q9-edge-cases.batch-lsh: Empty buckets (no docs, immediate return), hash collisions (multiple LSH codes → same bucket)
q9-edge-cases.adaptive: SIMD threshold (64+ tokens for benefit), Batch threshold (16+ docs for amortization)

rationale.examples: kindly_dedup (corpus gen), kindly-db (text search), log analysis, document indexing
rationale.speedup: 2-8× (proven pattern from SIMD hash capsules in atomic_capsule)

rationale.coupling: Tightly coupled to MinHashSignatureCapsule + LSH bucket structure

api.description: Extend DedupPipeline API with batch LSH queries (parallel bucket lookups)
api.integration: Minimal API change (add new method to existing struct)

simd-text.zero-cost: Inline functions, no allocations in hot path (Vec reuse)
simd-text.safety: 100% safe (portable_simd API, no manual SIMD intrinsics)

batch-lsh.pattern: rayon for parallel bucket queries (amortize overhead across batch)
batch-lsh.pooling: Thread-local Vec pool (avoid allocations, reuse buffers)

portable-simd.speedup: 2-8× (proven in SIMD MinHash, SIMD hash capsules)

inline-const.feature: Compile-time tuning (adaptive thresholds for SIMD vs scalar)

q13-simplicity.simd-text: Single function: hash_tokens_simd(text: &str) -> Vec<u64> (no complex state)
q13-simplicity.principle: Minimal API surface (one function per optimization, no unnecessary abstractions)

q14-resources.simd: 256-bit AVX2 registers (8× u32 or 4× u64 per operation)
q14-resources.parallel: 16 CPU cores (rayon work-stealing for batch LSH)
q14-resources.memory: Thread-local Vec pool (reduce allocations, ~16KB per thread)

q16-alternatives-rejected.per-doc-lsh: REJECTED: 1.3-2× overhead vs batch (sequential bucket queries)
q16-alternatives-rejected.unsafe-simd: REJECTED: portable_simd provides safe API with equivalent performance

q17-memory-efficiency.simd: In-place token hashing (zero-copy text scan, Vec reuse for output)
q17-memory-efficiency.batch: Thread-local Vec pool (avoid per-query allocations, reuse buffers across batches)
q17-memory-efficiency.target: Zero allocations in hot path (100% buffer reuse)

q20-error-handling.simd-text: Infallible (panic on invalid UTF-8 caught earlier in pipeline)
q20-error-handling.batch-lsh: Result<Vec<Cluster>> (LSH bucket errors propagate via Result)

q21-state-management.simd: Stateless function (no capsule state, pure computation)

q22-validation.simd: Property tests: 10K random texts, SIMD output == scalar output (determinism)
q22-validation.batch: Recall tests: Ground truth comparison, batch recall == sequential recall (no degradation)

q23-monitoring.simd: Throughput metric (tokens/sec, docs/sec), SIMD hit rate (64+ tokens)
q23-monitoring.batch: Batch size histogram, LSH hit rate (docs per bucket), throughput (docs/sec)

q25-documentation.format: Lean XML (architecture, performance claims, framework compliance)

q26-migration.simd: Drop-in replacement: Update corpus_gen() to use hash_tokens_simd() (1 line change)
q26-migration.batch: API extension: Add DedupPipeline::lookup_batch() method (backward compatible)

batch-memory-overhead.issue: Thread-local Vec pools add ~16KB per thread (16 threads = 256KB)

complexity-creep.fallback: If time-constrained, SIMD-only delivers 4× (Batch deferred to Week 3)
